name: Password reset link poisoned to an attacker-controlled host
requires: a password reset flow that emails a link containing a token
a mailbox we control to read what the target actually sends
a way to influence the host used to build the link, via Host or a forwarded-host header
questions: Does the reset email build its link from the request's Host header, X-Forwarded-Host, a Referer value, or a configured base that is only sometimes used?
Does the injected host actually appear in the link the victim receives, or is the link built from a server-side constant regardless of the header?
Does the token appear in the path or query of the poisoned link, so an attacker host would receive it and could then use it?
Does the reset flow validate the Host header against a configured allowlist on the request that triggers the email, or only on other routes?
Is the poisoned request a POST the attacker can force cross-site, or does it need a same-origin form with an anti-CSRF token?
Does the app accept a forwarded-host value only from a trusted proxy list, or from any client that sets the header?
Does the token remain valid after the attacker's host receives it, or is it bound to the requesting IP or session in a way that blocks reuse?
Is there a second poisoning vector, such as a language or template parameter that rewrites the link's domain?
false_positives: The Host header is reflected in the response body but the outgoing email uses a configured base URL
The link is poisoned but the token is bound to the victim's IP or session, so the attacker host cannot use it
The reset request requires an anti-CSRF token and same-site cookies, so the poisoned request cannot be forced cross-site
The email link uses a relative path that the victim's client resolves against the legitimate host
The token in the poisoned link is single-use and already consumed by the legitimate delivery
A forwarded-host header is ignored because the app only trusts it from a proxy address the attacker cannot spoof
poc_must_show: the exact reset request with the poisoned host header quoted, against the victim's identifier
the email as actually delivered, showing the link and the attacker host in it
the token extracted from that link, and evidence it is a live reset token for the victim's account
a control reset request without the header, showing the link points at the legitimate host
for full impact, proof the token is usable — or an explicit statement that using it was not attempted
impact_bar: the reset email delivered to a victim contains a link on an attacker-controlled host that carries a live token, shown from the actual delivered message
